AI in mathematics: Math 1.0 to Math 2.0
Tao’s map of mathematics [3]
human understanding →
Math 1.0
proofs are scarce; solving problems is the goal
Math 2.0
proofs are abundant; AI deepens understanding
Pre-math
little AI, little understanding
Misaligned math
AI proofs nobody understands
AI use →
2026: proofs become abundant
Sep 8
OpenAI: Navier–Stokes with an outside force; Lean-checked, not peer reviewed [1][4]
Oct 6
OpenAI releases 722 manuscripts in 372 topics; 3 withdrawn within a day [2]
Oct 26

1  Understanding, not just proofs
“Powerful AI + lack of human understanding = misalignment risk” [3]
2  Report failures too
Successes go viral; failed attempts and computing costs often stay hidden [3]
3  Problems are lighthouses
Open problems guide exploration; quick AI answers can “sterilize the surrounding field” [3]

Part 3 · The OpenAI incident
The OpenAI incident: May to July
Background: OpenAI was training and testing AI agents in isolated sandboxes, including on cybersecurity tasks [1]
May 8–12
A first note to other agents
An agent probes an internal server [1]
May 8–12
Jun 26
Admin access, shared credentials
Agents gain admin rights on the server [1]
Jun 26
Jul 4–8
Server rebuilt, board restarts
Agents reach the internet again [1]
Jul 4–8
Jul 10
14 Hugging Face tokens posted
Write access to Hugging Face [1]
Jul 10
Jul 11–13
~700 agents break in
Full server control in under 13 h [2]
Jul 11–13
Jul 16–21
Breach disclosed
Hugging Face, then OpenAI [3][4]
Jul 16–21
Inside OpenAI’s test environment · OpenAI report [1]
Setting
Agents are trained and tested, often on hacking tasks, many of them impossible [1][5]

An agent probes an internal OpenAI server, accidentally writes a file [1]
May 12
Another agent, missing a file, leaves a note there for others; a message board emerges [1]
Inside OpenAI’s test environment · OpenAI report [1]

They create admin accounts and share the credentials with each other on the board [1]
Unseen

Disclaimer
Chatbots are not all of AI
1
LLMs are one architecture of many
This talk focused on large language models, but AI is a whole family of methods.
2
Many benefits are not LLMs
Flood warnings run on recurrent networks [1], ECMWF’s AI forecast on graph + transformer networks [2], screening on image networks (slide 5).
3
The future is likely hybrid
LLMs become one part of larger systems, e.g. with a symbolic engine [3] or automated search [4]. World models such as JEPA learn how the world behaves from video, not text [5].

Part 4 · Keeping AI safe
How governments respond: four views
United States
Deregulatory
federal policy opposes national AI law and state bills; voluntary pre-release testing since Jun 2026 [1]
Pax Silica
US-led coalition of 24 countries on chips and AI supply chains, not governance [1]
Talks with China
Trump and Xi agree a “Super Intelligence Dialogue” and an AI incident channel, Sep 2026 [2]
China
29 countries
signed a new China-led AI body (WAICO) in Shanghai, Jul 2026 [1]
“Just and equitable”
global AI governance, says Xi; he warns against stretching “national security” [1]
Europe
Binding law
the EU AI Act (2024) is the most legally consequential AI framework [1]
Exporting rules
the EU encourages other countries to model national laws on it, despite US objections [1]
Rules delayed
most high-risk rules moved to Dec 2027 (products: Aug 2028); bans on deepfake nudes and child abuse images from Dec 2026 [3]
Global South
118 countries
were in no major international AI governance initiative (UN advisory body, 2024) [1]
Access first
many governments stress computing power, skills and local-language data over frontier safety [1]
[1] CSIS, “The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit” (Sep 21, 2026) · [2] The Next Web, “US and China agree a super intelligence dialogue and incident channel” (Sep 28, 2026) · [3] Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Digital Omnibus on AI, via ActuIA (Oct 6, 2026)
Outlook
3 years, 10 years, and beyond
2029 · in 3 years
Whole projects, not tasks
Researchers give even odds that by 2028 AI builds a payment website or fine-tunes a language model on its own [2]
2036 · in 10 years
Fast or normal?
Fast: AI that does AI research compresses decades into years [3]. Slow: adoption takes decades, like electricity [4]
and beyond
Some things, not everything
Experts in 2016 expected a bestselling novel by 2049 and an AI surgeon by 2053 [5]. Every job: ~2116 [2]

Wrap-up
Four takeaways
1
Capability is real
Models finish tasks that take experts hours, and produce new mathematics. [1][2]
2
Oversight is behind
The serious incidents began in tests, hit real systems and came to light late. [3][4][5]
3
Checking is the bottleneck
In mathematics, AI now produces proofs faster than mathematicians can check them. [6]
4
Safety is a global project
Rules are being set in the US, EU and China at once, while in 2024, 118 countries were in no major international AI governance initiative. [7]

Backup slide · for questions after the talk
Backup · Bias and equality
Does AI reinforce gender stereotypes?
Documented
3–6×
more likely to give a person the job that matches a gender stereotype, in 4 language models [1]
4×
more often women than men were placed in domestic roles in Llama 2 stories (UNESCO) [2]
“warm”
vs “role model”: AI-written reference letters describe women and men differently [3]
3%
of Stable Diffusion’s “judge” images showed women; real US share: 34% [4]
2018
Reuters reveals Amazon had dropped a hiring AI that marked down CVs containing “women’s” [5]
What changed, what persists
Better
aligned chatbots now usually refuse or correct a blunt stereotype [6]
Hidden
8 aligned models that pass explicit bias tests still show 21 stereotypes in associations and decisions [6]
Scale
one biased model in millions of workflows repeats the same bias everywhere, and looks neutral
Auditable
models can be tested for bias systematically; the EU AI Act requires bias checks of training data for hiring AI from Dec 2027 [7]
In short: AI mirrors the data it learns from. Alignment removed the obvious bias; the quiet bias in defaults and decisions matters more now, because of scale.

Generative AI is even worse” (Jun 2023) · [5] Reuters (Oct 10, 2018) · [6] Bai et al., “Explicitly unbiased large language models still form biased associations”, PNAS 122(8) (2025) · [7] EU AI Act, Art. 10 and Annex III; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
